title: 3D-CIMlet: A Chiplet Co-Design Framework for Heterogeneous In-Memory Acceleration of Edge LLM Inference and Continual Learning
problem: Edge AI hardware supporting both LLM inference and continual learning remains underexplored; 2D chiplet designs incur thermal and energy inefficiencies when integrating diverse memory technologies (RRAM, eDRAM) for accelerated inference.
motivation: Edge LLM inference demands heterogeneous compute-in-memory architectures with superior energy efficiency, requiring 2.5D/3D thermal-aware chiplet designs to combine multiple memory technologies and manage power density.
method: 3D-CIMlet stacks heterogeneous memory chiplets (using RRAM—resistive memory—and eDRAM—embedded dynamic RAM) in 3D architectures to accelerate AI language model processing on edge devices. The framework uses thermal simulations to predict where overheating will occur, then intelligently places each chiplet to minimize heat and energy waste. By matching different memory types to different processing tasks and considering thermal patterns during placement, it enables edge devices to both run trained AI models (inference) and continuously update those models with new data (continual learning).
key_novelty: The innovation is using thermal modeling to optimize how different memory technologies (RRAM and eDRAM) are arranged in 3D chip stacks for efficient edge AI inference and continual learning.
contributions: First thermal-aware modeling and co-design framework for edge-LLM CIM chiplet systems
Memory-reliability-aware chiplet mapping strategies for mixed-technology nodes
Up to 9.3x and 12x energy efficiency improvement in 2.5D and 3D vs 2D baselines
90.2% and 92.5% energy-delay product reduction for edge LLM continual learning
limitations: Not discussed; focus on modeling and simulation without silicon results.
primary_theme: Heterogeneous 3D CIM chiplets for edge LLM inference and continual learning
